claim: GLImageCache drops `repetition` on a cache hit, while GLTextureCache re-applies wrap for the same situation
subImageR8/subImageRGBA skip the kind check uploadR8/uploadRGBA enforce, so glyph bytes get written into a texture that belongs to an image

triage.scenario: an image is registered (or `upload`ed) under an id a dynamic glyph page later uses, e.g. `weasel-dyn-sdf-page-0`. `uploadR8` → `claimPage` sees the id taken by a non-page, warns "only the one made first is kept", and does nothing. But `dynamicPages.sync` (packages/font/src/dynamic/dynamicPages.ts:84-98) sees `cache.has(id)` true, skips the upload and patches: `subImageR8` looks the id up through `texture(id)` with no `pages` check and calls `writeSubTexture` with w×h single-channel bytes on the RGBA8 image texture. WebGL raises INVALID_OPERATION (or WebGPU a validation error) and nothing is written, or, for `subImageRGBA`, glyph texels overwrite the image's and its mipmaps are regenerated. Expected: the collision is settled one way, as `claimPage`/`collidesWithPage` settle it: the patch methods refuse a non-page id too.
triage.cause: page ownership checked on create, not on patch

claim: GLTextureCache: an id made by uploadR8/uploadRGBA has no source or premultiply record, so a later upload under it rewrites the texture with no collision warning

triage.scenario: Replacement allocation throws; after freeTransient, a request matching the previous attribute gets a handle to deleted GL resources
triage.cause: old resources released before fallible allocation

claim: GLTextureCache.sweep only runs on a registry version change, so a registered upload made after the frame's sweep for an id the registry no longer holds keeps its texture until some unrelated registration
The glyph-outline fill cache ignores the default open-fill rule, which the path fill cache rebuilds on
Marker head cache key conflates a bare marker key ending in `@` with a sized ref of the same stem
A font-atlas upload under an id already registered drops that id from the sweep, so its texture outlives the registry entry

triage.scenario: id `x` is drawn through `uploadRegistered` (added to `registered`), then a font atlas is uploaded under the same id with `upload`, which does `registered.delete(id)` and rewrites the texture (warned). When the texture registry later drops `x`, `sweep` never visits it, so the GPU texture lives until `free()`. Expected: the collision keeps one owner but the texture is freed once neither owner holds it.
triage.cause: ownership flag cleared rather than shared
